READABILITY.evidence: Names like ua/ub/va/vb, c0_0, idx0..idx3 and u_0..u_3 don't explain what they are. Raw fixed-point constants (-4865*rc - 9528*gc + 14393*bc + 8389120 >> 10, 32770, 28786) have no comment tying them to FFmpeg's RGB2YUV tables.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: rgbToYuv420OrNv is over 100 lines, and the YUV420P and NV12/NV21 branches repeat the same 4-tap vertical chroma blend in both SIMD and scalar form. The diff also commits build output (.zig-cache/h/*.txt, zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so).

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Magic constants are everywhere (8389120, 32770, 128, >>8). The dst_data[1].? / dst_data[2].? unwraps would panic on a NULL plane instead of returning an error. Scalar tails and the x+1<width guards are there.

C6-07-CASE1.evidence: SIMD loops have scalar tails (while cx < chr_w), odd widths are handled via x+1<width, and every plane uses its own stride via getRowPtrMut. But chr_h = height >> 1 rounds down, so with an odd height the last chroma row is never written. FFmpeg rounds up.

C6-07-CASE2.evidence: build.zig sets the x86_64_v3 target, perf-check loads the library and passes 58/58, and the code is single-threaded. I couldn't confirm the exported symbol list or precomputation in swscale_create from the truncated diff, and build artifacts are committed into the workspace.
